Original frames of source real_photos_v4 (kind=real_photo, photographic=True)

Existing label crops (traceability only, not a source of bottle shape)

Instance segmentation checkpoint that produces bottle masks

missing_optional_inputs.purpose: Existing label crops (traceability only, not a source of bottle shape)

labelling_distinguishes.note: Counts of identities whose slug carries the token. The catalog keeps these as separate identities; this stage does not merge them.

variant_only_identity_groups.note: Identities that become identical once vintage, volume and the trailing alcohol figure are stripped. A bottle silhouette cannot separate these; the label text or a vintage reader can.

identical_reference_photo.note: Two or more identities share one catalog photograph byte-for-byte. Neither a whole-bottle nor a label encoder can separate them, because the gallery holds the same image under both slugs.

dino_identity_holdout.note: Straddling groups are the ones whose natural hard negative lies on the other side of the generalisation holdout. Step 6 drops those pairs rather than leaking a reserved identity.

integrity.seen_identities_pulled_into_holdout_note: These identities are not reserved, but some of their images shared a provenance group with a reserved identity, so those images were held out with it. They still contribute their other images to training. This is the intended cost of grouping.

internal_validation_only: Any figure computed on the DINO synthetic validation split. That split already selected the current checkpoint, so it is internal validation, not an independent test.
evaluation_status.note: The test pool is held out from reranker training and from every selection decision. Two limits keep it from being a general verdict: it covers only the identities that happen to have been photographed, and it is the project-wide scanner check set, so each further use erodes its independence. Fresh sessions collected per the step 8 plan are the durable answer.

collection_rules: One shooting session is one observation. A burst of nearly identical frames does not count as variety.
Vary angle, distance, light and background across sessions, not inside one.
Photograph both members of a confusion pair, not only the one that loses.
Shoot the final-test material as separate sessions and keep it out of training entirely.
For pairs marked 'no visual difference exists', no amount of photography helps; the catalog entry has to be corrected.
